rows.en:
(I came to the beach with Michel,
but I bet his real goal is hitting on girls...)
rows.notes: Male. kaisuiyoku = a day swimming at the beach; nanpa = hitting on girls, as c06811.

rows.en:
(Geez! Speak of the devil...
Hm? Looks like it's the other way around,
and he's the one getting hit on.)

(But it kind of looks like
he's turning the invitation down...)
Sorry to keep you waiting.
I wasn't waiting that long, so it's fine.

But was that really okay, Michel?
Turning down that older lady's invitation?
rows.notes: Male. oneesama = an older woman; 'older ladies' as c10330.

rows.en: Yeah, well.
rows.notes: x4: Michel here (both genders); Alto in scd_fes_612, answering 'so you got brought to the dressing room too'. Works for both.

rows.en: Hmm, but......

I said it's fine. I came to hang out with you today.
Come on, let's hurry up and go swimming.

O-okay...
Then let's do that.

You're good at swimming too, huh, Michel.
I couldn't keep up with you at all...
rows.notes: Male. ha ga tatanai = no match for him.

rows.en:
You're still sloppy on the finish,
\p.
rows.notes: Both genders. tsume ga amai = weak at closing it out.

rows.en: Phew, I'm a little tired. Let's take a break.

By the way, Michel,
you don't want to hit on any girls today?

I told you earlier, didn't I?
I came to hang out with you today.
Well, if you say so...
I just want to be with you...
rows.notes: Both genders. Michel's fake confession (a tease, revealed at c10145).

rows.en: These feelings of mine are real...

Michel, calm down a second.
I mean, two guys together, that's...
there's all kinds of stuff......

Love has nothing to do with gender, right?
I... you're the one I......
rows.notes: Male. Deliberately cut off before the verb, as the Japanese (omae no koto ga...).

rows.en: Wh-whaaaaaaaat?!!
Pfft... Hahahahaha!

Seriously, you're so much fun to tease.
You crack me up.

Ah! You were messing with me again,
weren't you, Michel!

Haha, I'll go buy you a drink,
so cheer up already.
Geez! That Michel...

(But Michel not hitting on girls...
That really is rare.)

(Maybe what he said earlier
was actually kind of serious...)
(Haha, just kidding...)

(I came to the beach with Michel-kun,
but I bet his real goal is hitting on girls...)

(Geez! Speak of the devil...
Hm? Looks like it's the other way around,
and he's the one getting hit on.)
I wasn't waiting that long, so it's fine.

But was that really okay, Michel-kun?
Turning down that older lady's invitation?

O-okay...
Then let's do that.

You're good at swimming too, Michel-kun.
I couldn't keep up with you at all...

By the way, Michel-kun,
you don't want to hit on any girls today?

Michel-kun, calm down a second.
This is all so sudden...
I... you're the one I......
rows.notes: Female. Cut off before the verb, as c10143.

rows.en:
Ah! You were messing with me again,
weren't you, Michel-kun!
Ugh, honestly, Michel-kun!

(But Michel-kun not hitting on girls...
That really is rare.)
(Hehe, just kidding...)

(I came to the artificial island
to have fun with Michel today, but...)

(Michel's already getting hit on...
Huh? Looks like he turned her down.)
rows.notes: Male. 'her': c10171 names the inviter an oneesama.

rows.en:
Sorry for making you wait,
\p.

Nah, it's no problem.
But are you sure it was okay to turn her down?

I told you before, didn't I?
I came here to hang out with you.

Come on, I turned down a lovely lady's invitation
for this. Let's hurry up and have some fun
ourselves.

(All right! Today I'm gonna have
as much fun with Michel as I can!)

(I came to the artificial island
to have fun with Michel-kun today, but...)

(Michel-kun's already getting hit on...
Huh? Looks like he turned her down.)

No, it's no problem.
But are you sure it was okay to turn her down?

(All right! Today I'm going to have
as much fun with Michel-kun as I can!)

Yo, \p.
If you're free after this, want to go get some tea?

Sure, I don't mind...
Are you going to check out some new shop again?

Nah, there's something I wanted
to talk to you about...
rows.notes: Both genders. omae ni you ga aru.

rows.en: So, what did you want to talk to me about?

It's kind of embarrassing
to say it straight to your face, but...
(It's rare for Michel to hesitate like this...)
I wanted to thank you properly.
Thank me?

...What's gotten into you all of a sudden, Michel?
Did I do something to deserve your thanks?

If someone suddenly thanks you and you can't
think of any reason, sure, you'd be confused.

But hey, don't think too hard about it.
Just take it.
What do you mean? If you don't explain properly......

What I mean is, because you guys were by my side,
I was saved...
rows.notes: Both genders. omaetachi = you and the others.

rows.en:
Anyway, what I'm saying is,
I'm counting on you from here on too.

Yeah, that goes without saying.
And I'm counting on you too.
I see... It means a lot to hear you say that.

(Hmm, I don't really get it, but if Michel's
satisfied, I guess that's fine...)

Well then, now that I've said my thanks...
Guess I'll go out and hit on some girls.
(We were having a serious talk just a second ago...)

Today I'll teach you my never-fail techniques,
so learn them well before you go home.
Never-fail, huh...
Ah, you don't believe me, do you?
No, no, I totally believe you.
rows.notes: Male. Mock-polite desu/masu in the Japanese: sarcastic.

rows.en: Heh. Then let's go.

(Getting thanked by Michel
was a little embarrassing.)

(I hope Michel and I can keep
having fun hanging out like this from now on...)

uncertain: c10130 'Yeah, well.' (x4) is also Alto's reply in scd_fes_612; chosen to work for both.
c10143/c10161: deliberate cut-off before the verb ('I... you're the one I......'), as the Japanese omae no koto ga....
c10185: arigatou na rendered neutral 'Thanks.' since shared with the female scene.
c10200: player's mock-polite 'shinjitemasu yo' rendered sarcastic 'No, no, I totally believe you.'
c10129/c10156/c10171: oneesama = an attractive older woman ('older lady', as c10330 'older ladies').
